key_insight: A pathology foundation model with multiple instance learning graded Barrett’s esophagus dysplasia across institutions without stain normalization, achieving a macro-averaged AUC of 0.96.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more consistent dysplasia grading, particularly where disagreement over low-grade dysplasia complicates clinical decisions.
method: Analyzed 969 H&E-stained whole-slide images from four institutions.
Used expert-annotated patch classifiers to identify diagnostically relevant regions.
Applied attribute-aware multiple instance learning to classify slides as non-dysplastic, low-grade, or high-grade dysplasia.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective held-out test set of 130 slides, macro-AUC was 0.96 (95% CI 0.93–0.98), with 98% sensitivity and 81% specificity for dysplasia detection; no high-grade case was classified as non-dysplastic.
watch_item: Prospective validation in routine workflows is needed to establish generalizability and assess the impact of false-positive dysplasia classifications.
paper_title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
